disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set by regulation and can change. The Hunting and Trapping Regulations Synopsis is a summary, not the law; where it differs from the regulations, the regulations are the final authority. Always verify current regulations with the BC Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship before hunting or trapping. Trapping in British Columbia is governed by the Wildlife Act and the Wildlife Act Commercial Activities Regulation, B.C. Reg. 338/82. Trapping is on registered traplines or private property with written permission; a trapping licence and completion of an approved trapper education course are required.

license_summary.trapping_licence: A trapping licence is required (Wildlife Act s. 11, s. 40.1). The regional manager may issue one to a person who is a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident of Canada. Licences are issued through FrontCounter BC (online application, Basic or Business BCeID). A FWID (Fish & Wildlife ID, obtained through BC Hunting Online) is required to submit trapping reports.
license_summary.course: It is an offence to trap unless you have completed a trapper education course approved by the Director of the Wildlife Branch (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.10). Approved courses: B.C. since July 1, 1982; Quebec since July 1, 1988; Yukon, Alberta and Ontario since July 1, 1989. The BC Trappers Association delivers the 3-day Trapper Education Program (250-962-5452, info@bctrappers.ca). First-time applicants attach a photocopy of the course certificate.
license_summary.fees: Trapping licence $40.00 for one year / $200.00 for five years (GST included where applicable; Habitat Conservation Trust Fund surcharge included - $32 fee + $8 surcharge for one year; $160 + $40 for five years, B.C. Reg. 338/82 Schedule 2.02). Duplicate licence $10.00. Registered trapline transfer fee $50.00. Fur trader's licence $100.00; fur trader trading from a place of business in another province $400.00. (Synopsis p. 73; B.C. Reg. 338/82 Schedule 2.02.)
license_summary.licence_year: Annual trapping licences are valid from the later of July 1 of the year of issue or the issue date, to the following June 30 (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 2.04). A five-year licence runs to June 30 of the year five years after the year of issue (s. 2.04.1). The trapping licence year 2026-27 runs July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
license_summary.quotas: No bag limits are printed in the Provincial Trapping Seasons table, except the black bear quota of 2 in one licence year (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.20). Trapping is managed by registered traplines (Class 1 species: beaver, fox, marten, mink, muskrat, raccoon, skunk, squirrel, weasel) and regional regulation (Class 2: lynx, bobcat, wolverine, fisher, river otter; Class 3: wolf, coyote). Hunting bag limits for furbearers are in the regional General Open Seasons tables (see season rows).
license_summary.traplines: It is an offence to trap in any area unless you are the registered holder of the trapline for that area or are authorized by regulation or permit. Registration of a trapline on Crown land may only be granted to a person 19 years of age or older who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. No more than one trapline per person unless traplines are adjoining and a fur management plan is approved by the Regional Manager. Registration gives no proprietary rights in wildlife. A registered trapline must be actively trapped (or used by a licensed trapper, or temporarily discontinued with permission for up to two years); a trapline is unused if, within a year, the holder fails to take furbearers of $200 value or 50 pelts, unless that is unreasonable for the trapline. Transfer/relinquishment must be approved by the Regional Manager; transfer fee $50.00. Private-property trapping requires written permission of the owner/occupier. (Synopsis p. 72; B.C. Reg. 338/82 ss. 3.13-3.19.) Approximately 2,900 registered traplines in B.C. (BC Furbearer Management Guidelines).
license_summary.trap_check: A licence holder commits an offence by failing to examine: (a) every 72 hours, every holding or non-killing trap except an egg trap; (b) every 24 hours, every egg trap; (c) every 14 days, every killing trap or killing snare (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.05; Synopsis p. 71). On private property, holding/non-killing traps must be examined at least once every 24 hours. A trapped furbearing animal found alive must be immediately released or killed.
license_summary.harvest_report: Licensed trappers must submit a trapping harvest report each trapping licence year (July 1 to June 30), due 31 days after the end of the licence year - by July 31 (July 31, 2027 for 2026-27). A report is required even if no harvest occurred. Non-filing: the trapper cannot buy a licence, permit, limited entry hunting application or guide territory certificate until a report is submitted, and may be charged a $460 fine. Report online through WILD (BC Hunting Online) or on the form at any FrontCounter BC office. (Synopsis p. 72.)
license_summary.compulsory_reporting: Trappers must report within 15 days following the end of the trapping season: fisher in all MUs when trapped in an open season; wolverine in Regions 5, 6, 7A and 7B; bobcat in Region 2; wolf in Region 1 and MUs 2-5, 2-6, 2-11 to 2-16. (Synopsis p. 72.)
license_summary.compulsory_inspection: Furbearers trapped outside an open season (incidental) must be submitted (carcass and pelt) for Compulsory Inspection: fishers within 30 days of the kill; all others by June 30 of the licence year. These animals cannot be reclaimed. The pelt of a wolverine trapped in Region 3 during an open season must be submitted within 15 days after the last day of the continuous season (and before export if applicable). (Synopsis pp. 72-73.)
license_summary.royalties: Royalty must be paid to keep the pelt/skin of a furbearing animal lawfully taken under a trapping licence, unless sold to a licensed fur trader. Royalty is 3% of the average auction price for that species over the preceding three years. Current schedule (gov.bc.ca, as of January 14, 2026), per pelt: beaver $1.03, black bear $8.69, bobcat $11.29, coyote $0.68, fisher $1.94, fox $0.73, lynx $5.33, marten $2.08, mink $0.32, muskrat $0.07, otter $1.40, raccoon $0.21, skunk $1.38, squirrel $0.04, weasel (ermine) $0.25, wolf $9.62, wolverine $16.18. An Assigned Trapper Number (ATN) is required by the fur trader when accepting, exporting and selling fur, and when paying royalties. (Synopsis p. 73.)
license_summary.export_cites: Any raw fur or skin shipped out of the province for commercial purposes must be accompanied by an Export Permit (Synopsis p. 72). A CITES Export Permit is required to export out of Canada all bears, cougar, lynx, bobcat, wolf, sea otter, or river otter or parts of these animals (Synopsis p. 16).
license_summary.certified_traps: A person using killing traps for beaver, bobcat, fisher, lynx, marten, muskrat, river otter, raccoon or weasels, or restraining traps for beaver (cage traps), bobcat, lynx or wolf is required by law to use only species-specific traps included in B.C.'s trapping regulations that have been certified under the Agreement on International Humane Trapping Standards (Synopsis p. 72; B.C. Reg. 338/82 Schedule 3.04; certified-trap lists Synopsis pp. 74-75). See the 'aihts' section of this dataset.
license_summary.hunting_furbearers: Furbearers may also be hunted under a hunting licence in regional General Open Seasons (bobcat, lynx, coyote, wolf, wolverine, raccoon, skunk; see hunting season rows in this dataset for Regions 2, 5, 6, 7A, 7B and 8). Cougar and black bear are big game hunted under the Hunting Regulation (B.C. Reg. 190/84); their hunting seasons were not transcribed in this pass. Hunting rows for Regions 1, 3 and 4 were not verified in this pass (see known_gaps).
license_summary.permission: Trap only on your registered trapline, or on private property with the written permission of the property owner or occupier. Trapping in ecological reserves is prohibited; trapline tenure in provincial parks, conservancies and recreation areas is subject to the Park Act and requires a Park Use / Resource Use Permit.
license_summary.report_violation: Report All Poachers and Polluters (RAPP), 24-hour hotline 1-877-952-7277 (1-877-952-RAPP), or #7277 on a cellphone. Online: forms.gov.bc.ca/environment/rapp/. Reports go to the Conservation Officer Service.

verification.confirmation_notes: Trapping seasons cross-checked between two independent extractions of the official 2026-2028 Synopsis: the full synopsis PDF (Trapping Regulations section, p. 76 Provincial Trapping Seasons table) and the regional chapter PDFs (Regions 1, 2, 5, 6, 7A, 8; Region 7B chapter read inside the full synopsis PDF). The two extractions agree on every shared trapping row. Season dates are printed as recurring month/day ranges in the 2026-2028 synopsis (effective July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028) and are converted here to 2026-27 instances (open dates in 2026, close dates in 2027 where the season wraps the year). February 28, 2027 is the last day of February 2027 (2027 is not a leap year), verified by calendar check. Licensing, fees, trap-check intervals, compulsory reporting/inspection and royalties cross-checked between the synopsis (pp. 71-73) and the gov.bc.ca trapping pages and BC Laws (B.C. Reg. 338/82). The 2026 wolverine Region 6 amendment was verified in B.C. Reg. 97/2026 (effective July 1, 2026). Furbearer hunting rows were transcribed from the regional General Open Seasons tables for Regions 2, 5, 6, 7A, 7B and 8 only. Latin names are as stated in B.C. Reg. 168/90 s. 16 (and Schedule D for sea otter) except for badger, whose name is standard taxonomy.
known_gaps: Furbearer hunting rows for Regions 1 (Vancouver Island), 3 (Thompson) and 4 (Kootenay) were not extracted - the regional PDFs for Regions 3 and 4 and the furbearer rows of Region 1 could not be read before a browser rate limit stopped the extraction. Raccoon hunting in Region 7B was not located in the Peace General Open Seasons extraction (flagged as a gap, not confirmed absent). Resolution: re-read the Region 1, 3 and 4 chapter PDFs and the Region 7B PDF directly.

Fisher season conflict: the 2026-2028 Synopsis Provincial Trapping Seasons table (p. 76) lists a fisher season ONLY for MUs 6-19 to 6-27 and Region 7B, but Schedule 3.08 of B.C. Reg. 338/82 carries MU-level 'No open season' entries for fisher in parts of Regions 3 and 5 (e.g. MUs 3-12 to 3-20, 3-26, 3-34 to 3-37, 3-42 to 3-46), which implies a broader base season in Schedule 3.07. The dataset follows the synopsis table. Resolution: full read of the current consolidated Schedules 3.07/3.08 on BC Laws and/or confirmation from the ministry.

Full Schedule 3.07/3.08 matrix (the law) was not read cell-by-cell; the dataset rests on the Synopsis p. 76 reprint plus spot checks (wolverine 2026 amendment; fisher 3.08 entries). Resolution: read the consolidated B.C. Reg. 338/82 Schedules 3.07/3.08 on BC Laws and diff against the synopsis table.

Spotted skunk: designated a fur bearing animal (B.C. Reg. 168/90 s. 16(y)) but no species-specific season row exists anywhere; whether the table's 'Skunk' season legally covers spotted skunk is unverified. Modelled as closed. Resolution: ministry confirmation or a reading of the 'Skunk' row definition in Schedule 3.07.

Badger's precise protecting instrument was not pinned down: no open season and red-listed/Endangered status are verified, but no regulation section naming badger was located in this pass. Resolution: BC Laws search for 'badger' in B.C. Reg. 338/82 / the Closed Areas Regulation and a full read of the ministry badger brochure.

Region 6 wolf hunting bag limit: the numeral was not legible in the text extraction of the Region 6 General Open Seasons table. The row is included with no bag limit and a note. Resolution: visual check of the Region 6 PDF.

Full model-by-model transcription of the certified-trap lists (Synopsis pp. 74-75) not done in this pass (structure and species categories only); the Trapping Methods matrix (p. 75) per-cell assignments could not be reliably reconstructed from the PDF text extraction. Resolution: visual transcription from the PDF, or from the Fur Institute of Canada certified list.

Minimum age for a trapping licence itself: unverified. The gov.bc.ca apply page states no age and Wildlife Act s. 40.1 states only citizenship/permanent residency; 19+ is verified for trapline registration and for a fur trader licence, not for the trapping licence. Resolution: read the full text of Wildlife Act ss. 11/40.1 and the application form's eligibility block.

Arctic fox, kit fox and grey fox are designated fur bearing animals (B.C. Reg. 168/90 s. 16(h)-(j)) but do not occur in B.C. and have no season rows; they are not modelled as species entries. No action needed unless the clone needs a 'designated but absent' note.

Timezone split: the dataset uses America/Vancouver throughout. The Peace Region (7B) is on Mountain Standard Time year-round (America/Dawson_Creek) and the Creston area of Region 4 is America/Creston (MST, no DST); northwest open/close times in those MUs are one hour off if read as Pacific Time. The clone needs the split or a gap note.

Black bear hunting seasons (General Open Seasons, regional chapters) and cougar hunting seasons were not transcribed; cougar is big game, not a furbearer, and has no trapping season. If the clone shows hunted big game, these are separate tasks.

In-season corrections: the synopsis notes corrections are published online at www.gov.bc.ca/hunting. This dataset is a snapshot of the synopsis as read 2026-11-15; in-season changes after that date are not reflected.

Trapline boundary data: the dataset references Regions and Management Units only. Individual trapline boundaries (~2,900 registered traplines) and MU boundaries are a separate dataset task, not scoped here. Minimum viable: let the trapper pick their region/MU from a list.

aihts.note: British Columbia implements AIHTS through the Wildlife Act Commercial Activities Regulation, B.C. Reg. 338/82, s. 3.04 and Schedule 3.04, which lists the lawful traps by species and trap position; the Synopsis (pp. 74-75) reprints the certified-trap lists. A 'certified trap' is one listed in Schedule 3.04 for that species and position. The Fur Institute of Canada maintains the national certified-trap list (updated July 22, 2026); B.C.'s lists are drawn from it. AIHTS was agreed in 1997 and ratified by Canada in June 1999. Since the 2007-2008 season B.C. trappers have been required by law to use only AIHTS-certified traps for the mandated species; the requirement is phased in species by species once enough trap types are certified and trappers are notified.
aihts.models_note: This pass captured the mandate structure and species categories from the Synopsis (pp. 74-75) and the Trapping Standards page, not the full model-by-model lists. The pp. 74-75 tables could not be transcribed with dataset-grade reliability from the PDF text extraction (multi-column interleaving). Full transcription from the PDF (or from the FIC list) is a defined follow-on task. Certification is not the same as current manufacturing: several certified models are legacy/discontinued. Do not present the certified list as a shopping list without a retailer-availability check.

certified_killing_traps.note: Underwater or on land; list on Synopsis p. 74.
On land only; and underwater only: any jaw-type trap (body gripping or foot-hold) set as a submersion set that exerts clamping force and keeps the animal underwater.
Covers least, long-tailed and short-tailed weasel.

certified_restraining_traps.note: Live cage traps (Breathe Easy, Comstock, Dam Beaver, Ezee Set, Hancock, Koro 'Klam').
Foot snares and specified soft-catch / laminated / offset foot-hold models.

trap_rules: Only certified traps may be used for the mandated species/positions (Synopsis p. 72; B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.04 and Schedule 3.04).

It is an offence to trap within 200 m of a dwelling unless using, on land, a live box trap or egg trap, or on/in water a Conibear not larger than size #330 or equivalent, foot-hold traps not larger than size #2, or submarine traps (Synopsis p. 71; B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.06).

Trap check: holding/non-killing traps every 72 hours (24 hours on private property); egg traps every 24 hours; killing traps and killing snares every 14 days (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.05; Synopsis p. 71).

It is an offence to use a foot-hold trap with teeth or other projections on the jaws; to use a killing snare on land unless it has a locking device, is designed for squirrels/hares, or is a mechanically powered killing snare; to use snare wire heavier than 20 gauge or braided wire unless licensed/authorized to trap; to set spring poles or running poles unless equipped with a killing trap; to use a trap with a spearing device; to use a Conibear larger than (not including) #220 for land sets within any municipality (Synopsis p. 73).
Egg traps may only be used by a person holding a valid trapping licence, and the trap must be securely fastened or anchored so a caught animal cannot drag it away (Synopsis p. 73).

Fisher exclusion boxes are required for listed 120-size traps set on land in MUs 3-30, 3-31, 5-1, 5-2, 5-12, 5-13 and 5-14: box at least 17 inches long (outside), entry hole no more than 56 mm (2-1/4 in) in diameter, side slot at least 10 in long and no more than 1 in high (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.04.1; Synopsis p. 73).
Wolf foot-hold traps must be solidly fastened with no more than 60 cm of chain (Synopsis p. 75, footnote 1).
Muskrat submerging sets smaller than size #1 1/2 require a minimum 150 g weight securely attached (Synopsis p. 75, footnote 2).
In Region 5 it is an offence to set a killing snare to trap wolves or coyotes within 10 m of where bait is placed (Synopsis p. 73).
Killing snares in the Kootenay Region are limited to Dec 1 - Mar 31 for wolf (Provincial Trapping Seasons table footnote, p. 76).

It is an offence to trap wildlife using a firearm from one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise the following day, unless using a firearm to kill a furbearing animal caught in a trap on a registered trapline (Synopsis p. 71).

A trapped furbearing animal found alive must be immediately released or killed; a trapping licence does not authorize possession of live wildlife, and live trapped furbearers must not be transported and released elsewhere without a permit (Synopsis pp. 71-72).

It is an offence to cause or allow dogs to pursue furbearers under the authority of a trapping licence; electronic or recorded calls may be used for trapping wolf, coyote, bobcat or lynx only (Synopsis p. 73).

Future restriction under consideration: restricting box/cage traps for live-trapping raccoons and restraining traps for live-trapping coyotes to AIHTS-certified traps only, starting in the 2028-2029 trapping year (Synopsis p. 72).

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: 72 hours for holding/non-killing traps; 24 hours for egg traps (raccoon).
check_interval.killing: 14 days for killing traps/killing snares on a trapline (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.05).

canada_only.tenure: Registered traplines on Crown land (holder must actively trap to the regional manager's satisfaction or risk cancellation); private-land trapping needs the owner's written permission.
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: None found - no trap owner-ID marking requirement in the sources searched (follow-up pass, Nov 17); identification runs through licence/tenure and pelt seals instead. BC's Assigned Trapper Number is used on fur-sale/export/royalty paperwork, not on traps.
canada_only.royalty: 3% of the 3-year average Canadian auction price per pelt, payable by a trapper who keeps a pelt (not payable if the pelt is sold to a licensed fur trader); due to the regional manager by March 31 following the year taken (B.C. Reg. 338/82 s. 3.09). [R1 s.5; R2 Item 5]
canada_only.nuisance_route: Paid route exists - General Wildlife Permit (Permit Regulation, B.C. Reg. 253/2000): s. 2(b) hunt/trap/kill on own property in/out of season; s. 2(c)(iii) hunt/trap/kill on others' property for problem wildlife (application via FrontCounter BC listing professional qualifications; records due within 21 days after permit expiry). Schedule C species need no permit with owner permission. [R1 s.4]
canada_only.harvest_reporting_and_sealing: Compulsory reporting within 15 days after season end for listed species, plus a general compulsory report of furbearers killed (Reg. 338/82 ss. 3.16, 3.16.1); compulsory inspection/carcass submission for wolverine, lynx, bobcat and wolf by region/MU and for fisher in any MU with an open season; fur traders must submit lynx pelt measurements. [R1 s.5]
